Quick diagnostic from the runtime side (prelim):

Observations:
- We see a 2.6x increase in tail latency on requests matching the long-context tag (avg seq_len ~2100) for the variant v2.3-quant8 which was part of the rollout.
- Kernel selection logs show a fallback to the slower attention kernel for ~18% of v2.3 requests under the current batch/seq mix — this was not present in the previous stable model.
- Batching metrics: Culver's per-tenant batching window widened from 6ms to ~22ms under the v2.3 traffic slice, which increased end-to-end queuing.

Hypothesis: a micro-architecture interaction (quantized attention path + sequence-length distribution) is increasing per-token latency for long contexts, causing backpressure and widened batching windows which drive p95/p99 up even though error rate remains low.

Immediate mitigations we can do:
1) Hotfix routing rule: pin Culver's traffic to v2.2-stable (rollback for tenant) — fast and reversible.
2) Tweak per-tenant batching threshold and max-window for Culver to limit queuing.
3) If we rollback, collect a controlled canary run where we inject long-context queries to validate tail behavior.

I'll run the rollback unless you object. ETA ~8m for rollback and ~10m for verification.

Jonas
Staff Engineeer, Serving Runtime

We apologize for the impact. I will chair the post-mortem and include the kernel team. If Culver execs want a dedicated briefing, we are available this afternoon.
